C06 is a close thematic and rhetorical analogue concerning restoration of flood-control appropriations, while C25 is strongly connected to New England water-resource planning and federal-state coordination but uses different administrative machinery and structure.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the Conference recommends a $3,400,000 supplemental appropriation for fiscal year 1956 to start construction of authorized flood control projects on which planning has been completed","parent_excerpt":"I am transmitting today supplemental estimates of appropriations for flood control work for the fiscal year 1952","explanation":"Both frame the response around a supplemental fiscal-year appropriation for flood-control construction."},{"child_excerpt":"Appropriation requests... to accelerate Corps of Engineers' flood control activities... are now undergoing analysis in connection with our overall budget recommendations. These recommendations will go to the Congress","parent_excerpt":"the agencies of the Executive Branch have reviewed the situation to see whether any parts of our flood control work should be accelerated... the work of the Army Corps of Engineers... is a vital part of that program","explanation":"The same administrative sequence appears: disaster-driven executive review, possible acceleration of Corps work, and submission of funding recommendations to Congress."},{"child_excerpt":"When the reports of the extent of the damage are in, we shall... take into account whatever modifications in the above program are necessary to meet whatever emergency that now confronts us.","parent_excerpt":"The recent floods... require us to re-examine our plans.
